rows.proof: BOARD OF ASSESSORS, page 38 of the FY2016 annual town report. TWO tables. TABLE 1, `Assessor's Account for Exemptions and Abatements`: Description | FY2016 | FY2015 | FY2014 | Prior Years | Totals. THREE ROW IDENTITIES CLOSE TO THE CENT -- overlay less deficits less charges to 6/30/2016 less released to surplus is the total balance, for each of FY2016 ($140,212.29 - $118,903.55 = $21,308.74), FY2015 ($207,330.39 - $133,262.09 = $74,068.30) and FY2014 ($145,256.60 - $123,225.96 = $22,030.64) -- and the Total Balance row foots across to its own printed Totals column, $21,308.74 + $74,068.30 + $22,030.64 + $26,760.88 = $144,168.56. `-0-` is the page's EXPLICIT ZERO and is read as 0.00, not as a missing figure. TABLE 2, `New Growth Revenue`, seven fiscal years 2010-2016: Fiscal Year | Added Valuation | Tax Rate | New Revenues | Change (%). It states no total and the verifier's identity grammar handles only addition and subtraction, so its two relations are computed here and recorded rather than asserted, and its rows are published as `line`. CHANGE (%): six of the seven close -- each year's New Revenues against the year below it. FY2013 DOES NOT: $321,862 against FY2012's $448,111 is MINUS 28.17 per cent and the page prints `28.17`. The magnitude is right to two decimals, so this is a dropped minus sign in the published document. ADDED VALUATION x TAX RATE / 1000 = NEW REVENUES: six of the seven close within $6 (the valuations are printed in whole dollars, so the product is the rounded figure and not the rounding of the product -- FY2016 is out $5.52 and FY2014 $1.24). FY2011 DOES NOT, and it is out by $142,000: the page prints Added Valuation $3,291,045 at a rate of 14.20, which gives $46,733, against a printed New Revenues of $188,732. $188,732 requires an added valuation of $13,291,045 -- the printed figure with a leading 1. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: which figure of the FY2011 pair the town got wrong. $13,291,045 reproduces the printed revenue exactly, which is why a dropped leading digit is the obvious reading, but nothing on the page or in this report tests it and the revenue could be the wrong figure instead. Both are recorded as printed and neither is corrected. THE PRIOR YEARS COLUMN PRINTS ONLY A TOTAL BALANCE. Read off the page: the Assessor's Overlay, Overlay Deficits, Charges to 6/30/2016 and Released to Surplus rows print figures under FY2016, FY2015 and FY2014 and NOTHING under Prior Years (`140,212.29 207,330.39 145,256.60` at x=219/292/364, and the Prior Years cell at x=443 is empty on all four rows); only the Total Balance row prints $26,760.88 there. So the vertical identity has nothing to check for Prior Years -- absent is not zero, and asserting 0 - 0 - 0 - 0 = 26,760.88 reports the town's document as broken when the document simply prints no components for the older years. THE PAGE'S OWN HORIZONTAL IDENTITY IS WHAT COVERS IT, and it is in `fy2016-p38-assessors-balances.csv`: the Total Balance row foots across to its printed Totals cell, $21,308.74 + $74,068.30 + $22,030.64 + $26,760.88 = $144,168.56, so the Prior Years figure is asserted there rather than left unchecked. THE SPLIT IS A LIMIT OF THE CHECKER, NOT OF THE PAGE: verify_page_reads.py applies a declared row identity to every row that prints its WHOLE, and has no way to exempt a row that prints none of the PARTS -- the mirror of the case it does handle.

rows.read_by: claude-opus-5 reading the PAGE'S OWN EMBEDDED BITMAP. pdfplumber reports ONE word of text on PDF page 40 (the folio) and one DeviceRGB image, 660x1080 at 78 dpi with an /SMask, so the page is a photograph and no text layer exists. The bitmap was taken straight out of the PDF stream -- the stream is a raw FlateDecode DeviceRGB sample array with NO container, so `get_data()` cannot be handed to PIL and `Image.frombytes('RGB',(660,1080),...)` was used with the stream's own /Width, /Height and /ColorSpace, then composited over white through its /SMask (without that composite the page renders as coloured text on black). The result was rotated 90 degrees clockwise -- the page is printed sideways -- and read at 3.2x in three column bands, each band carrying the FUND NAME column pasted beside it so no row could be mis-paired. NO RECOGNITION WAS USED and the OCR rows previously held for this page were discarded rather than reconciled.
rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG TRUST FUNDS` FY 2016 fund balance reconciliation, PDF page 40 of the FY2016 annual town report: the first of three pages of one statement (pp.40-42), 22 funds in three named sections, in NINE money columns. THE COLUMNS ARE NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER, WHICH WAS READ AND WRITTEN DOWN, verbatim: ACCOUNT NUMBER | FUND NAME | FY 2016 BEGINNING PRINCIPAL | FY 2016 BEGINNING EARNINGS | FY 2016 CONTRIBUTE TO PRINCIPAL | FY 2016 NET EARNINGS | FY 2016 DISBURSE FROM PRINCIPAL | FY 2016 TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS | FY 2016 ENDING CASH VALUE | FY 2016 UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS | FY 2016 ENDING MARKET VALUE. It is spelt BEGINNING, with two Ns, on both of its columns -- not the BEGINNNING of some other years. This is the nine-column layout FY2014 established and FY2016 ACCEPTS it: every column present, in the same order, and no tenth. THE ACCOUNT NUMBER COLUMN IS PRINTED AND EMPTY on every row of this page, so no account number is recorded; the fund name is the key and the 22 names are distinct. TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS is printed in parentheses, in red, where it is not nil, and is stored NEGATIVE as printed. WHAT PROVES IT -- THE PAGE'S OWN ARITHMETIC, TWICE PER ROW AND ONCE PER COLUMN. (1) EVERY FUND ROW closes twice: its six components sum to ENDING CASH VALUE, and that plus UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS is ENDING MARKET VALUE -- 44 independent assertions across the page. (2) EVERY SECTION closes to the SUBTOTALS row the page prints beneath it, in all nine columns -- 27 more. All 71 close to the cent, with no tolerance declared. A single wrong digit anywhere breaks at least two of them.

rows.proof: THE DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE, pages 44-46 of the FY2016 annual town report: 39 bond issues against fiscal years 2017 to 2047, printed as PRINCIPAL / INTEREST / TOTAL per issue per year, with GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL, GRAND TOTAL INTEREST and TOTAL DEBT rows at the foot of each page. THE EXTENT: page 44 carries FY2017-FY2028, page 45 FY2029-FY2039, page 46 FY2040-FY2047 plus a TOTAL column. PAGE 46 ALSO REPRINTS FY2030, FY2031 AND FY2032, which page 45 already carries -- the figures are identical and they are transcribed as `line` rows, NOT summed, so no year is counted twice. The 31-year span is 2017-2047 with no gap. WHAT CLOSES, AND IT IS THE WHOLE PAGE. 228 per-issue-per-year identities assert principal + interest = that issue's TOTAL. Independently, the 228 issue-years sum across all three pages to the TOTAL column page 46 prints: principal $52,186,684 against a printed $52,186,686, interest $23,849,141 against $23,849,136, and the two together $76,035,825 against a printed TOTAL DEBT of $76,035,822 -- the last stated here rather than asserted, because THREE issue-years print principal and interest and no TOTAL cell, so the per-year total column cannot sum to it and a check on it would be a check on what the page omits. A DECLARED TOLERANCE OF $6, AND THE REASON. This schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts that carry cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts. The evidence that it is rounding and not a misread is the DISTRIBUTION, not the size: of 228 per-issue identities every single break is exactly plus or minus one dollar and there is no break of any other magnitude anywhere on the three pages; the largest residual in the whole read is $1726370 on $76,035,822. A misread digit in figures of this size costs $10 or more far more often than $1, and could not produce breaks that are all +/-1 with both signs. The tolerance is NOT set to the residual: it is $6 against a worst case of $1726370. ONE DOCUMENT DEFECT, NOT RECONCILED. On page 46 the TOTAL column for `MASS WATER POOL 9*` is printed $3,171,339 while the same column prints principal $3,043,839 and interest $546,204, which sum to $3,590,043 -- out by $418,704, and $418,704 is exactly that issue's FY2024 principal, the last year it pays. So the printed issue total appears to omit one year. It is recorded as a `line` and is NOT part of any sum above; which figure the town intended is NOT established.
